title: Proxy capacity

panels.title: Score
panels.description: Users held through the 5-minute hold. 0 = the run stopped early.

panels.title: p95 at score
panels.description: p95 latency over the 5-minute hold that set the score. Limit: 500 ms.

panels.title: Errors at score
panels.description: Failed requests over the 5-minute hold that set the score. Limit: 1%.

panels.title: Peak req/s
panels.description: Highest 5 s rate of successful requests in the run.

panels.title: Stopped by
panels.description: What went wrong on the last failed probe: the step just above the score.

panels.title: Peak proxy RSS
panels.description: Most memory the proxy process used in the run. The box has 2 GB; the kernel kills the proxy near that.

panels.title: CPU / request
panels.description: Median µs of proxy-box CPU per successful request (ignores moments under 100 req/s). Lower = more efficient.

panels.title: Score per version
panels.description: Users held by every saved run, lowest to highest. Ignores the time picker.

panels.title: Runs
panels.description: Every saved run in results/ (ignores the time picker). Click a version to open its run.

panels.title: Users and connections
panels.description: Simulated users (target) vs TCP connections mload actually has open to the proxy. A gap means connections are being refused or dropped.

panels.title: Successful requests per second
panels.description: Successful requests per second (mload counts only requests that got a response). Failures are in the errors panel.

panels.title: Latency of successful requests (log scale)
panels.description: Dashed lines are the limits: p95 must stay under 500 ms (orange), p99 under 1 s (red).

panels.title: Errors (% of requests; limit 1%)
panels.description: Line: failed requests as % of all requests in each 5 s window (the rule is < 1% over the hold). Bars: number of failed requests per 5 s (right axis).

panels.title: Proxy box CPU per request (µs, log scale)
panels.description: CPU time the proxy box spent per request: busy CPU (without steal and I/O wait) ÷ mload's successful req/s. Lower = a more efficient proxy. Background services are paused, so this is almost all the proxy. Skipped while under 100 req/s (e.g. right after an OOM restart), where it means nothing.

panels.title: CPU steal per server (probe invalid above 5%)
panels.description: Time a server's CPU was taken by other VMs on the same host. Above 5% the numbers depend on the neighbours, not on the proxy, so the probe should be marked invalid.

panels.title: What ran out first: CPU or memory (% of the proxy box)
panels.description: CPU busy and memory used on the proxy box, both as % of what the box has, plus p95 latency (right axis). The line that reaches 100% first is the limit. In v0, CPU reaches 100%, requests pile up (p95 climbs), and memory follows until the kernel kills the proxy.

panels.title: Proxy CPU by kind
panels.description: 1 vCPU. 'steal' is time taken by other VMs on the same host.

panels.title: Proxy box memory: where the 2 GB goes
panels.description: Stacked to the box's total RAM. When 'available' reaches ~0 the kernel kills the biggest process (the proxy). 'kernel: slab' is mostly per-connection kernel memory (sockets, TCP state): ~7 KB per open connection, outside Go's control.

panels.title: Out-of-memory kills and proxy up
panels.description: An OOM kill shows as a bar; 'up' drops to 0 when the proxy process is gone.

panels.title: Pressure (time spent waiting)
panels.description: Linux PSI: % of time tasks waited for memory or CPU. Rising memory pressure comes before an OOM kill.

panels.title: Go memory: live data vs garbage
panels.description: Stacked: everything the Go runtime holds. 'live data' is what the last GC found still in use; 'garbage' is dead objects waiting for the next GC. With GOGC=100 the garbage may grow until the heap reaches the dashed 'GC heap goal' (~2x live). GOMEMLIMIT (red dashed, only when set) caps it.

targets.legendFormat: heap: free, not returned to OS

panels.title: Goroutines
panels.description: net/http uses about one goroutine per client connection, plus some per backend connection.

panels.title: Allocation rate and GC heap goal
panels.description: More allocation means more GC work. With GOGC=100 the heap may grow to ~2x live data before a GC.

panels.title: GC: cycles per second and share of CPU
panels.description: How often the GC runs, and what share of the Go program's CPU it takes.

targets.legendFormat: % of Go CPU spent on GC

panels.title: Connections and open files
panels.description: Each user = 1 client connection; the proxy also opens backend connections. The red line is the open-file limit (65,535): the proxy can't hold more files than that.

panels.title: Dropped and failed connections
panels.description: Non-zero accept-queue drops mean new connections arrive faster than the proxy accepts them.

panels.title: Network traffic
panels.description: Bytes per second through the proxy box's network card.

panels.title: Retransmitted segments
panels.description: TCP segments sent again because they were lost. Should stay near zero on a quiet network.

panels.title: CPU busy per server
panels.description: The backend and load generator should stay well below 100%, so the proxy is the limit. Dashed line: the load generator must stay under 70% for a probe to count.

panels.title: Memory used per server
panels.description: RAM in use per server (total − available), plus mload's own memory on the load generator (dashed).

description: Capacity runs of the $12 reverse proxy challenge. Click a version in Runs to open its run; the Overview tiles follow the time picker.
